# dpprfs

> Improves the computed solution to a system of linear equations when the.

<section class="intro">

coefficient matrix is symmetric positive definite stored in packed format,
and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dpprfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dpprfs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dpprfs(
    order,
    uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    AP,
    AFP,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → info: integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | specifies whether 'upper' or 'lower' triangle is stored |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `AP` | `Float64Array` | in | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | original symmetric matrix in packed storage |
| `AFP` | `Float64Array` | in | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | Cholesky-factored matrix in packed storage (from dpptrf) |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix (column-major) |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of B |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (improved on exit) |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of X |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output forward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output backward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 3 * N` |  | workspace array (length >= 3*N) |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | integer workspace array (length >= N) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AP`: The upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.
- `AFP`: The triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^T \, U$ or $A = L \, L^T$, as computed by DPPTRF/ZPPTRF, packed columnwise in a linear array in the same format as A (see `AP`).
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by DPPTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dpprfs.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    AFP, strideAFP, offsetAFP,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → integer
```

Improves the computed solution to a real system A * X = B where A is symmetric positive definite in packed storage and provides error bounds.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | specifies the operation type |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | the number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. |
| `AP` | `Float64Array` | in | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `AP` |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AP` |
| `AFP` | `Float64Array` | in | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideAFP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `AFP` |
| ↳ `offsetAFP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AFP` |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `B` |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `X` |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ 3 * N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `IWORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AP`: The upper or lower triangle of the symmetric matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.
- `AFP`: The triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^T \, U$ or $A = L \, L^T$, as computed by DPPTRF/ZPPTRF, packed columnwise in a linear array in the same format as A (see `AP`).
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by DPPTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dpptrf from '../../dpptrf/lib/index.js';
import dpptrs from '../../dpptrs/lib/index.js';
import dpprfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dpprfs';

// 3x3 SPD matrix in upper packed storage: [ 4 2 1; 2 5 3; 1 3 6 ]
const AP = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 2.0, 5.0, 1.0, 3.0, 6.0 ] );
const AFP = new Float64Array( AP );

// Factorize
dpptrf.ndarray( 'upper', 3, AFP, 1, 0 );

// Right-hand side
const B = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 ] );

// Solve
const X = new Float64Array( B );
dpptrs.ndarray( 'upper', 3, 1, AFP, 1, 0, X, 1, 3, 0 );

// Refine solution
const FERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const BERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 9 );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 3 );

const info = dpprfs.ndarray( 'upper', 3, 1, AP, 1, 0, AFP, 1, 0, B, 1, 3, 0, X, 1, 3, 0, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'X:', X ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'FERR:', FERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'BERR:', BERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DPPRFS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DPPRFS improves the computed solution to a system of linear equations when the coefficient matrix is symmetric positive definite and packed, and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution.

</section>
